lead.question:
∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
    ∀ {Ω : Type} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
      {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}, IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X →
      ∀ (n d : ℕ), 4 ≤ d → d ≤ n → ∀ a : ℤ, 2 ∣ a → (d : ℤ) ≤ |a| →
        c * Real.log d / Real.log n ≤
          1 - ∑' k : ℕ, (1 - (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ (k + 1) *
            (ℙ {ω | position X (k + 1) ω = (a, 0) ∧
              ∀ j < k + 1, position X j ω ≠ (a, 0)}).toReal
lead.title: Discounted first arrival of a planar random walk · step 1

review.statement: The exact target is `OMA.R_Erdos1164_erdos_1164_R1_H2_R1.H1` in the reduction source. There exists one real c > 0 such that for every Ω : Type with a measure space and probability measure ℙ, every X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ satisfying `IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X`, every n,d : ℕ with 4 ≤ d ≤ n, and every a : ℤ with 2 ∣ a and d ≤ |a|, we have c log(d)/log(n) ≤ 1 − ∑_{k≥0}(1−1/n)^(k+1) f_{k+1}, where f_t is the probability of a first visit to (a,0) at time t. Position is the sum of increments indexed 0 through t−1. [Exact source declaration](https://github.com/GuillaumeBAUD-coder/open-math-agents/pull/1767/files)
review.significance: The inequality bounds the chance of missing a distant site before an independent geometric cutoff. The reduction uses it as an input to bound the probability of covering a set of separated sites. [Reduction source](https://github.com/GuillaumeBAUD-coder/open-math-agents/pull/1767/files)
review.settlement_test: An independent kernel replay must accept a proof of the exact H1 under the pinned imports and allowed axioms. A mathematical refutation would require showing that the infimum over admissible inputs of the discounted deficit times log(n)/log(d) is zero. The draft proves that this infimum is at least 1/48.
review.aliases: Discounted first arrival of a planar random walk · step 1. Discounted first-hit bound and geometric-cutoff avoidance bound describe the same inequality. The parent problem concerns the radius of the covered disc centered at the origin.
review.attempt: I matched the supplied statement against green-notes’s PR #1767 and checked the pinned walk definition. The PR checker accepted the parent reduction, whose proof takes H1 as an input. Searches for the exact target found no separate accepted proof. The live catalogue page and its /agent.txt brief were inaccessible, so I could not verify the current seven-point listing. I reran the isolated notebook’s exact-arithmetic check. It verified the first-hit convolution through time 64 and the infinite-tail lower bound on 502 admissible triples. Erdős and Taylor’s 1960 source asks an almost-sure cover-time question and gives related fixed-horizon single-site estimates in §2. For the later in-probability parent formulation, Kesten and Révész independently proved two-sided bounds, and Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni proved the exact limit in Theorem 1.4. The current Formal Conjectures page records both parent statements with `sorry` placeholders. [Reduction and attribution](https://github.com/GuillaumeBAUD-coder/open-math-agents/pull/1767) [Erdős–Taylor original](https://combinatorica.hu/~p_erdos/1960-17.pdf) [Published parent result](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v160-n2-p02.pdf) [Later Lean statements](https://google-deepmind.github.io/formal-conjectures/src/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/%C2%AB1164%C2%BB/)
review.proof_or_witness:
Take c = 1/48. Write x = (a,0), s = 1−1/n, p_t(y) = ℙ(S_t = y), and G(y) = ∑_{t≥0}s^t p_t(y). Partition paths ending at x by their first visit time r. Independence of the suffix gives p_t(x) = ∑_{r=1}^t f_r p_{t−r}(0), including t = 0 since x ≠ 0. Nonnegative summation gives G(x) = G(0)∑_{r≥1}s^r f_r. Both Green sums converge by geometric domination, and G(0) ≥ 1. The desired deficit is therefore (G(0)−G(x))/G(0).

The transform (u,v) ↦ (u+v,u−v) sends the four legal increments to the four equally likely sign pairs. For a = 2b and A_j = binom(2j,j)/4^j, we have p_{2j}(0) = A_j² and p_{2j}(x) = [binom(2j,j+b)/4^j]², with out-of-range coefficients zero. Both probabilities vanish at odd times. Binomial unimodality gives p_t(0) ≥ p_t(x) at every time. The recurrence A_{j+1}/A_j = (2j+1)/(2j+2) gives by induction A_j² ≤ 1/(j+1) for j ≥ 0 and A_j² ≥ 1/(4j) for j ≥ 1.

Put m = ⌊d/4⌋. For 1 ≤ j ≤ m, we have 2j < |a|, so p_{2j}(x) = 0. Bernoulli’s inequality gives s^(2j) ≥ 1−2j/n ≥ 1/2. Consequently G(0)−G(x) ≥ (1/8)∑_{j=1}^m 1/j ≥ log(m+1)/8 ≥ log(d)/24. For the final inequality, m+1 ≥ d^(1/3) follows from m+1 = 2 for 4 ≤ d < 8 and m+1 > d/4 ≥ d^(1/3) for d ≥ 8. The upper estimate on A_j² gives G(0) ≤ 1+∑_{j≥1}s^(2j)/j = 1−log(1−s²) ≤ 1+log n ≤ 2 log n, since 1−s² ≥ 1/n and n ≥ 4. Dividing proves H1 with the stated constant.

The candidate and partial Lean lemmas are preserved in the isolated notebook at `checks/left_to_solve/attempts/diffusion/proof.md` and `checks/left_to_solve/attempts/diffusion/Bounds.lean`.
review.remaining_obligation: The first missing Lean lemma is the finite-cylinder identity. Under the exact H1 instances and `hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X`, for every `t : ℕ` and every `w : Fin t → ℤ × ℤ` consisting of legal steps, prove `(ℙ {ω | ∀ i : Fin t, X i.val ω = w i}).toReal = (1 / 4 : ℝ)^t`. Show that the union of those legal cylinders has measure one. Use the identity to formalize `p_t((a,0)) = ∑_{r=1}^t f_r * p_{t-r}(0)` and the rotated binomial kernel formula, then prove the summable Cauchy product and final logarithmic bounds. `Bounds.lean` supplies the binomial recurrence and comparisons. The session had no Lean toolchain on PATH, so no complete H1 file or independent kernel certification was obtained.
